(NYSE: GBX) (“Greenbrier”), a leading international supplier of equipment and services to global freight transportation markets, today reported financial results for its fourth fiscal quarter and year ended August 31, 2026. Fourth Quarter and Full Year Highlights • Q4 new railcar orders for 3,400 units valued at $600 million and deliveries of 3,600 units resulted in new railcar backlog of 14,000 units with an estimated value of $2.1 billion as of August 31, 2026. • Completed programmatic restoration work on approximately 2,200 railcars during fiscal 2026; Not included in backlog, these units support volume in our manufacturing plants and fixed cost absorption. • Q4 Net earnings attributable to Greenbrier were $9 million, or $0.27 per diluted share. Results include $4 million ($0.12 per share) of expense related to facility rationalization costs, net of tax and noncontrolling interest. • Q4 Core net earnings attributable to Greenbrier were $12 million or $0.39 per diluted share. • Core EBITDA was $72 million in Q4, or 12% of revenue. • Fiscal 2026 Net earnings attributable to Greenbrier were $79 million, or $2.49 per diluted share. Results include $4 million ($0.11 per share) of expense related to facility rationalization costs, net of tax and noncontrolling interest. • Core net earnings attributable to Greenbrier in fiscal 2026 were $83 million, or $2.60 per diluted share. • Fiscal 2026 Core EBITDA was $300 million, or 12% of revenue. • Owned lease fleet grew 23% in fiscal 2026, to 20,900 units, maintaining strong utilization of 98%. • Returned $56 million to shareholders in fiscal 2026 through dividends and share repurchases. • Board approved quarterly dividend of $0.34 per share, payable on December 2, 2026 to shareholders of record as of November 11, 2026, representing Greenbrier's 50 th consecutive quarterly dividend. - More - Greenbrier Reports Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2026 Results (Cont.) Page 2 “Order activity improved in the fourth quarter despite tariff uncertainty in our North America markets, particularly in tank cars, triggering delays in long-lived railcar investment decisions,” said Lorie L. Tekorius, CEO and President. “The first sequential increase in backlog since fiscal 2024 represents a pivot by freight shippers toward moving goods by rail in North America. Our lease fleet grew by 23% to nearly 21,000 railcars at year end, with utilization of 98%, further establishing a recurring revenue base supporting results across market conditions and industry cycles.” Tekorius added, “Rail traffic increases and elevated diesel prices have boosted inquiries in North America early in fiscal 2027, as freight shippers seek increased access to rail. Our focus on operational execution, cost management and disciplined growth of the lease fleet continues. About Greenbrier Greenbrier, headquartered in Lake Oswego, Oregon, is a leading international supplier of equipment and services to global freight transportation markets. Through its wholly-owned subsidiaries and joint ventures, Greenbrier designs, builds and markets freight railcars in North America, Europe and Brazil. We are a leading provider of freight railcar wheel services, parts, maintenance and retrofitting services in North America. Greenbrier owns a lease fleet of approximately 20,900 railcars that originate primarily from Greenbrier's manufacturing operations. Greenbrier offers railcar management, regulatory compliance services and leasing services to railroads and other railcar owners in North America. Financial Metric Definitions Core EBITDA, Core net earnings attributable to Greenbrier and Core diluted earnings per share (EPS) are not financial measures under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). These metrics are performance measurement tools used by rail supply companies and Greenbrier. You should not consider these metrics in isolation or as a substitute for other financial statement data determined in accordance with GAAP. In addition, because these metrics are not measures of financial performance under GAAP and are susceptible to varying calculations, the measures presented may differ from and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies. We define Core EBITDA as Net earnings before Interest and foreign exchange, Income tax expense, Depreciation and amortization and the impact associated with items we do not believe are indicative of our core business or which affect comparability. We believe the presentation of Core EBITDA provides useful information as it excludes the impact of financing, foreign exchange, income taxes and the accounting effects of capital spending and other items. These items may vary for different companies for reasons unrelated to the overall operating performance of a company’s core business. We believe this assists in comparing our performance across reporting periods. Core net earnings attributable to Greenbrier and Core diluted EPS exclude the impact associated with items we do not believe are indicative of our core business or which affect comparability. We believe this assists in comparing our performance across reporting periods. ###
